chunks: Via his chain from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a boy of ten years – can he make the Hajj? He said: upon him is the Hajj of Islam if he has begun getting nocturnal emissions, and the same is the case for the girl – Hajj is upon her if she has begun menstruating.
ai.seo_question: At what age does Hajj become obligatory for children in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Faqih clarifies that the age of ten serves as the primary indicator for the obligation of Hajj, contingent upon the physical signs of puberty: nocturnal emission for boys and menstruation for girls. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that while ten is the baseline age, the actual binding obligation is triggered by the onset of biological maturity, ensuring the pilgrim possesses the necessary capacity. This ruling underscores the practical application of 'bulugh' (pubescence) in determining religious accountability for major acts of worship.

en.ammaar-muslim: 7. [7/106] al-Faqih: Via his chain from Safwan from Ishaq b. Ammar who said:

I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about a boy of ten years – can he make the Hajj? He said: upon him is the Hajj of Islam if he has begun getting nocturnal emissions, and the same is the case for the girl – Hajj is upon her if she has begun menstruating.
